source: NCERT Class XI, Themes in World History, Ch. 7 (Paths to Modernisation).

sections.heading: 1. The Theme — East Asia
points: The chapter compares the **different paths to modernisation** taken by **China and Japan** in the 19th–20th centuries.
Both faced Western pressure but responded very differently — Japan modernised rapidly, China through revolution and turmoil.

sections.heading: 2. Japan — The Meiji Restoration
points: Japan was long ruled by the **Tokugawa shogunate** (the emperor was a figurehead); society had samurai, peasants, artisans, merchants.
American **Commodore Perry (1853)** forced Japan to open to trade.
The **Meiji Restoration (1868)** restored the **emperor** and launched rapid modernisation: slogan **'fukoku kyohei' (rich country, strong army)**.
Reforms: modern **army and navy, industrialisation, railways, Western education, a constitution (1889), banking**; Japan became an **imperial power** (defeated China 1895, Russia 1905).

sections.heading: 3. China — From Empire to Republic
points: China (the **Qing dynasty**) faced humiliation: the **Opium Wars (1839–42)** with Britain, unequal treaties, loss of Hong Kong, foreign 'spheres of influence'.

Reform and rebellion followed: the **Taiping Rebellion**, the reform efforts, and the **Revolution of 1911** which ended the monarchy — **Sun Yat-sen** founded the **Republic** (his 'Three Principles': nationalism, democracy, socialism/people's livelihood).
The **Chinese Communist Party (CCP)** under **Mao Zedong** grew; after civil war and war with Japan, the **People's Republic of China was founded in 1949**.

sections.heading: 4. Contrasting Modernisation
points: **Japan** modernised under its **own leadership**, preserving traditions while adopting Western technology — a top-down, relatively peaceful transformation.
**China** modernised through **revolution** — the collapse of empire, communism, and Mao's programmes; later economic reforms under **Deng Xiaoping** opened the economy.
Both became major powers, but by very different routes.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Meiji Restoration (1868) = restored emperor, modernised Japan; slogan 'rich country, strong army'.
Commodore Perry (1853) forced Japan to open to the West.
Opium Wars (1839–42) humiliated Qing China; Britain took Hong Kong.
1911 Revolution ended Chinese monarchy; Sun Yat-sen founded the Republic (Three Principles).
People's Republic of China founded 1949 under Mao Zedong; Deng Xiaoping later opened the economy.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Meiji Restoration (1868)** restored the **emperor** and modernised Japan.
**Commodore Perry (USA, 1853)** forced Japan open — not Britain.
**Sun Yat-sen** founded the Chinese Republic (1911); his **Three Principles**.
The **People's Republic of China** was founded in **1949** under **Mao Zedong**.
